content: Apply a gel containing phenylephrine and witch hazel externally to the clean, dry area affected by hemorrhoids. This gel can be applied up to four times daily, particularly at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may aggravate hemorrhoids. When using the product for the first time, puncture the foil seal with the top end of the tube’s cap. For individuals under 12 years of age, use of this product should be based on a careful assessment of whether the benefits outweigh the risks. For those aged 12 years or older, the gel should be applied externally to the clean, dry hemorrhoidal area, following the same frequency and timing guidelines. There are no reported adverse reactions associated with the use of this product. However, if ingested, witch hazel may cause nausea, vomiting, or liver damage. The product should not be used by individuals with hypersensitivity to phenylephrine, witch hazel, or any inactive components. It is intended for external use only and should not be used orally. Caution is advised for individuals with heart disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, or prostatic hypertrophy due to the presence of phenylephrine. Discontinue use and consult a physician if hemorrhoids worsen or fail to improve within seven days. Additionally, stop using the product if symptoms such as bleeding, allergic reactions, redness, irritation, swelling, pain, or other adverse effects develop or worsen. The gel should not be inserted into the rectum using a mechanical device or fingers. This product is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning that its effects on fetal development are uncertain, and it is unknown whether it is excreted in breast milk. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using over-the-counter medications.
